free_tier.stated: A membership whose monthly fee buys a fixed block of GPU hours, which is the cheapest denominator found anywhere among evaluated providers. Quoted: HyperAI Pro at USD 4.99 per month includes 30 GPU hours per month usable on a single RTX 5090, so a fully used month is USD 0.1663 per 32 GB GPU-hour, with no carry-over: 'Any remaining quota will be cleared at the beginning of the following month'. On-demand rates on the same site: RTX 5090 32GB USD 0.35/hr, RTX PRO 6000 96GB USD 0.80/hr, H100 PCIe 80GB USD 1.80/hr. Basic is quoted at USD 0.00 to get started with 20 GB of storage and a free CPU container of 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM.

free_tier.stated: Free tier storage is 'Free 20 GB + Extra 50 GB, totaling 70 GB'. But the 70 GB is explicitly a Pro benefit ('Upgrade to HyperAI Pro, Unlock More Benefits .. 3.5× more storage: Free 20 GB + Extra 50 GB, totaling 70 GB'). So free is 20 GB, and 70 GB costs $4.99/month.

egress.terms: Not metered on the free tier; storage tiers are the paid dimension (a discounted tier table exists for scalable storage).

record.tooling: Web console + app.hyper.ai notebooks; no documented S3/CLI blob API found. Storage is attached to notebooks rather than exposed as a bucket.
record.chaining: 20 GB per account is too small to multiply usefully; 500 accounts per 10 TiB.
record.limits_note: 20 GB free, 2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM, 2 h max continuous CPU runtime (8 h on Pro), 30 h/month compute on Pro. Storage is workspace-scoped, not bucket-scoped.
record.reliability_note: Small aggregator-style GPU marketplace; the storage is a notebook side-car, so data tied to a workspace that may be reclaimed.

evidence.proved: read live: 'Run experiments and light workloads on our Free CPU—2 vCPU · 4 GB RAM'; Pro block: '3.5× more storage — Free 20 GB + Extra 50 GB, totaling 70 GB'
